title: Signed within-visit systolic drift does not improve albuminuria prediction in an independent NHANES cycle
abstract: A fixed signed first-to-third systolic drift feature was tested beyond mean BP, within-visit SD and clinical covariates for concurrent elevated random urine ACR. Weighted logistic models were trained in NHANES 2009–2010 (n=5022) and tested in the separately sampled 2011–2012 cycle (n=4367). Test log-loss improvement was -0.00005974 (95% conditional rescaled-PSU bootstrap interval -0.00017530 to 0.00006495); AUROC declined from 0.733103 to 0.732871. Flexible-baseline, medication-negative and order-reversal checks did not establish incremental benefit. This negative result is specific to this representation and outcome, not evidence that all reading-order information is absent or a diagnosis of persistent kidney disease.
